parts.prompt: Briefly describe the purpose of the **_integration_** phase in secure software development. Name one risk if security is not properly addressed during this phase.

marking_criteria.criterion: Demonstrates a clear understanding of the integration phase; accurately describes its purpose and provides a relevant security risk.
Shows some understanding; may provide a partial description of the phase or a somewhat relevant risk.
Provides minimal or unclear explanation; may mention a phase or risk with little detail or relevance.

parts.sample_answer: The integration phase involves combining software components into a complete system and verifying that security measures function correctly across them. If security is not addressed, components may interact in unexpected ways, creating vulnerabilities. For example, one risk is that an insecure API between modules could allow unauthorised access to sensitive data.

questions.title: End User Influence (SA, TKS 2025)
questions.label: SA
questions.stimulus: A mobile payment app is used by both tech-savvy professionals and elderly users with limited digital experience. The company is redesigning the app's security features after discovering that many users disabled them due to confusion.

parts.prompt: Describe two secure design solutions the developers could implement to ensure that users of varying experience levels can confidently use the app without compromising its security.

marking_criteria.criterion:
Describes two relevant and secure design solutions appropriate for users with varying experience levels

Clearly addresses both usability and security in context

Describes one relevant and secure design solution

OR

Describes two solutions with limited detail or relevance
Shows some understanding of usability or security in app design

parts.sample_answer: To improve usability without reducing security, developers could introduce simplified onboarding that walks users through setting up essential security features with visuals and plain language. This would help less experienced users avoid disabling protections out of confusion. Additionally, enabling adaptive security—where the app quietly increases protection (e.g., requesting verification for large sum transfers)—ensures advanced users are not frustrated by constant prompts, while still maintaining safety. These strategies ensure that all users can operate the app securely and with confidence.
